claims.text: HEA multilayer protective coatings resist time-dependent plastic deformation.
Suppression of dislocation motion at layer interfaces causes the resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation.
High lattice distortion and chemical complexity in the HEA layers govern the suppression of dislocation motion.
The proposed coatings contain alternating chemically complex HEA layers and simpler metallic or ceramic layers.
Applying a constant load at elevated temperature induces creep in the coatings.
Layer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Lattice mismatch contributes to the barrier to dislocation motion at layer interfaces.
Chemical complexity contributes to the barrier to dislocation motion at layer interfaces.
High lattice distortion and chemical complexity create localized stress fields in HEA layers.
Localized effects associated with lattice distortion and chemical complexity reduce dislocation mobility.
The combined effects of HEA-layer lattice distortion, chemical complexity, and layer interfaces suppress creep deformation.
Multilayer HEA coatings will have significantly lower creep rates than single-layer HEA coatings under identical conditions.
Multilayer HEA coatings will have significantly lower creep rates than conventional-alloy or ceramic multilayer coatings under identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies only over temperature and stress ranges in which coating creep occurs.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the multilayer structure remains intact without delamination.
Evidence is limited regarding the specific contribution of interfaces to creep resistance in HEA multilayer coatings.
